120ft raises €576,000 for container-based robotic microfactories

The three-container concept targets small assembly batches, with brands paying for completed products.

Humanoids Daily ↗15 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1

A shared small factory

Stockholm startup 120ft disclosed €576,000 from 22 angel investors to develop humanoid-operated assembly facilities in three 40-foot containers. They divide preparation, assembly, and inspection with packing. The company plans to own and operate the facilities while customers pay per finished product.

Starting with constrained work

The proposed service starts at batches of 100, with brands retaining designs and component suppliers. Initial pilots target rigid parts below 5 kg joined by screws or press-fits; cables, flexible materials and gluing come later. Factory OS is intended to connect AI, robots and automation to assembly workflows.

Programming time is not cycle time

The company says skill-programming time fell from seven weeks in 2025 to seven hours in 2026, with seven minutes targeted for 2027. Its curve is an outlook rather than measured time-series data, and does not describe manufacturing time per item. Success rates and human-assistance frequency remain undisclosed, leaving commercial quality and economics to be demonstrated.
